title: SKEW stores every x87 step of z^3 while SKEW.P evaluates in binary64, drifting 1 and 4 ULP on (1,2,3,5)
statement: In Excel 16.0 builds 20430 and 20527, both SKEW and SKEW.P require at least 3 numeric inputs with nonzero variance (#DIV/0! otherwise). SKEW stores every x87 PC64-to-PC53 step of two-pass mean, sumsq, s = sqrt(sumsq / (n - 1)), each z = (v - mean) / s, sum(z^3), and (n / ((n - 1) * (n - 2))) * cubes (yielding 0x3fe8173e09af74be on =SKEW(1,2,3,5), 1 ULP low), whereas SKEW.P evaluates in binary64 (yielding 0x3fdbd1516b638101 on =SKEW.P(1,2,3,5), 4 ULP high, and #NAME? under compat-1).
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0 build 20430 (4,508/4,508 SKEW full-bank and 120/120 pinned rows) and 16.0.20527.20088 (2,800/2,800 SKEW.P full-bank rows and prefix_metadata rows 204-205).

correct.how: 100-digit decimal (4 / 6) * sum(((v - 11/4) / sqrt(35/12))^3), rounded to nearest binary64
